title: Components & JSX
summary: Describe a screen as small reusable pieces.
points: A React component is a capitalized function that returns renderable UI. Keep rendering pure: do not save data or mutate outside state during render.
JSX describes elements. Use braces for JavaScript expressions, className for CSS classes, and htmlFor to connect a label.
Return one root element or a fragment. Close tags, including self-closing inputs.
The starter uses a Vite browser app with a React root and TypeScript. It is an exercise in client UI, not a server or account system.
Function components compose other components. Extract a component around a coherent responsibility rather than every line of markup.
output: Rendering <Welcome /> shows a heading Learn React and a paragraph One small step.
mistake: Calling a state setter unconditionally while rendering can create a render loop.
challenge: Build a PlannerHeader component with a heading and a short description. Check the heading order.

title: Props, composition & types
summary: Pass information down and actions back up.
points: Props are inputs from a parent. Treat them as read-only; do not mutate a prop object or array.
TypeScript props types describe required and optional inputs. Destructure props in the component parameter.
Pass callback props to ask the parent to update shared data. Calling a callback is different from mutating a prop.
children lets a component wrap other content. ReactNode describes many renderable values, including text and elements.
A component should have a clear contract. Keep state ownership in the nearest component that must coordinate it.
output: <Badge count={3} /> renders 3 tasks. Omitting count is a TypeScript error.
mistake: Mutating a prop bypasses the owner’s update flow and can make renders inconsistent.
challenge: Create a typed TaskRow with task and onToggle props. Let its parent own the task array.

diagram.caption: Pass information down and actions back up.

title: Lists, keys & conditional UI
summary: Make empty, filtered, and changing lists predictable.
points: Use map to render a list and filter to derive a view. Keep the complete source array intact.
Keys identify siblings across renders. Use a stable task ID rather than an array index when items can move or disappear.
A key is used by React; it is not passed through as an ordinary prop. Pass an id prop separately if the child needs it.
Render an explicit empty state. A ternary can choose between an empty message and the task list.
Be careful with count && <List /> because zero can render as 0. Use count > 0 or an explicit branch.

rows: Explain a list with no items

output: An empty tasks array shows No tasks yet. Otherwise each task title appears in a list.
mistake: Generating a random key while rendering causes items to be recreated instead of preserving identity.
challenge: Render two tasks, remove the first, and confirm the second keeps its identity. Add a distinct message for an empty filtered view.

diagram.title: Lists, keys & conditional UI
diagram.caption: Make empty, filtered, and changing lists predictable.

title: State, events & update queues
summary: Change the next render without mutating the current one.
points: useState stores component state and gives you a setter. Call hooks at the top level of a component or custom hook.
An event handler sees the state snapshot for its render. Calling a setter requests a future render; it does not rewrite that local snapshot.
When the next value depends on the previous value, use a functional updater such as setCount(c => c + 1).
Copy arrays and objects when updating. Use map, filter, and spread instead of changing the current state in place.
Pass a function to onClick. Writing onClick={save()} calls save during render instead of waiting for a click.
output: Starts at 0. Each click adds 2 because both updaters use the pending value.
mistake: Calling setCount(count + 1) twice in one handler usually requests the same replacement value twice.
challenge: Add a completion toggle using map and a functional updater. Verify the old task object remains unchanged.

diagram.title: State, events & update queues
diagram.caption: Change the next render without mutating the current one.

title: Controlled forms & accessibility
summary: Make typing, submission, and feedback work together.
points: A controlled text input receives value and an onChange handler that updates it. Keep its value a string from the first render.
Use checked and onChange for a controlled checkbox. Its text value is not the checked state.
Handle form onSubmit and preventDefault so Enter and the submit button share one path.
Associate labels with controls and announce outcomes using a status region. Native required and maxLength help, but validate trimmed input too.
Keep event types appropriate: React form events and DOM events are different types. Extract currentTarget values while handling the event.
output: Typing updates title. Submitting spaces shows Enter a title; a nonblank title shows Ready.
mistake: Starting an input value as undefined and later supplying a string switches between uncontrolled and controlled behavior.
challenge: Build an add-task form with a visible label, trimmed validation, and an announced success message. Test Enter.

diagram.title: Controlled forms & accessibility
diagram.caption: Make typing, submission, and feedback work together.

title: Shared state & derived views
summary: Keep one source of truth for components that agree.
points: Lift shared state to the nearest common parent. Pass data and callbacks to children.
Compute counts and filtered tasks from the task array during render instead of synchronizing duplicate state with an effect.
A component’s state is tied to its place and identity in the tree. A changed key can intentionally reset that state.
Prop drilling is sometimes simple and appropriate. Context is useful for genuinely shared distant consumers, not mandatory for every prop.
A reducer can centralize related transitions when many handlers update the same data. Keep reducers pure and return new state.
output: Counts and the visible list update together whenever tasks or view changes. This is a contextual fragment, not a standalone program.
mistake: Saving only shown tasks would discard tasks hidden by the current filter.
challenge: Give a summary, filters, and list one shared task array. Remove any state that can be calculated from it.

diagram.title: Shared state & derived views
diagram.caption: Keep one source of truth for components that agree.

title: Effects, cleanup & browser sync
summary: Synchronize external systems only when needed.
points: Effects connect a committed UI to an external system such as storage or a subscription. Calculating a filtered array does not require an effect.
List every reactive value used by the effect in its dependencies. Do not suppress the dependency rule to hide stale data.
Return cleanup to undo a subscription, listener, or other ongoing operation before it is replaced or unmounted.
Development StrictMode can run an extra setup/cleanup cycle. Make synchronization safe to repeat and do not disable checks to hide a bug.
Separate user actions from synchronization. Sending a request because a user clicked a button normally belongs in that handler.
output: After commit, the browser title reflects count. Cleanup restores the previous title before a replacement setup or unmount.
mistake: An effect that changes a dependency unconditionally can keep triggering itself.
challenge: Synchronize a task count into the document title and verify cleanup. Keep filtering outside effects.

diagram.title: Effects, cleanup & browser sync
diagram.caption: Synchronize external systems only when needed.

title: Async data & request states
summary: Make loading, errors, and retry visible.
points: Represent idle, loading, success, and error explicitly. A single empty array cannot explain whether a request failed or has not started.
Check HTTP status and validate parsed data. TypeScript annotations do not guarantee a remote JSON shape.
For interaction-triggered loading, use the event handler and disable repeat submission while a request is pending.
For effects that fetch on changing inputs, abort or ignore stale responses during cleanup so old results cannot overwrite newer ones.
Show empty success separately from failure, provide retry, and preserve useful existing user data when requests fail.
output: Resolves to an array of strings for valid JSON. Rejects on network, HTTP, parse, or shape failures.
mistake: A late response for an old selection must not overwrite the latest selection’s results.
challenge: Implement idle/loading/success/error views for practice ideas. Test a missing file, invalid JSON, empty array, and retry.

diagram.title: Async data & request states
diagram.caption: Make loading, errors, and retry visible.

title: Refs, focus & custom hooks
summary: Reuse behavior while keeping the screen accessible.
points: useRef stores a mutable value between renders without requesting a new render when it changes.
Attach a ref to an input and focus it after an event when appropriate. Null-check current because the element can be absent.
Use state for values that affect the visible UI. A ref alone will not update a displayed counter.
A custom hook is a function named useSomething that composes hooks. Each call has its own state; sharing logic does not automatically share data.
Call hooks in a stable order at the top level. Avoid calling them inside loops, event handlers, conditions, or after conditional early returns.
output: Clicking Focus input moves keyboard focus to the labelled input.
mistake: Changing ref.current does not schedule a render, so it cannot replace state for visible task counts.
challenge: After deleting a focused task, move focus to a useful remaining control. Extract reusable behavior only when it has a clear contract.

diagram.title: Refs, focus & custom hooks
diagram.caption: Reuse behavior while keeping the screen accessible.

title: Build a component planner
summary: Bring typed state, components, and recovery together.
points: The starter splits the header, form, task list, and ideas panel into typed components. The parent owns the task array.
Tasks use stable IDs, immutable changes, derived filters, safe text interpolation, and labelled native controls.
A guarded storage initializer validates existing data. Synchronization skips unreadable storage until the user chooses a temporary list.
Practice ideas load from a bundled JSON file. Loading, empty, failure, and retry are visible; this is not a live recommendation service.
Type checks, model tests, keyboard checks, and a production build complement each other. Extend the project with editing and due dates before considering accounts or a backend.
output: The checkbox reflects its task and requests an update by stable ID. The parent supplies the actual update.
mistake: Do not use dangerouslySetInnerHTML for task titles. Plain JSX text safely displays text that looks like markup.
challenge: Extend the React starter with editing and due dates. Verify reload, filtering, failure recovery, keyboard use, and narrow screens.

diagram.caption: Bring typed state, components, and recovery together.
